newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank profits up, buy-back ruled out.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank profits up, buy-back ruled out.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland said on Wednesday that a strong performance from its British banking operations helped fuel a 23 percent increase in first half profits.
But the Edinburgh-based bank ruled out following others in the industry and using capital to buy-back shares.
Speaking at a press conference Royal Bank's chief executive George Mathewson said that the bank saw many opportunities to invest in new and existing businesses.
"We don't anticipate we'll accumulate excess capital," he added.

While Royal Bank has made no secret in the past of its interest in acquiring a building society if a suitable opportunity arose, Mathewson that at the moment that looked unlikely with current prices "pretty hard to justify".

The bank reported pre-tax profits of 369 million pounds ($603.3 million) for the six months to March 31, up from 301 million pounds the previous year. It will pay an increased interim dividend of 6.2 pence.

Mathewson said a 24 percent increase in pretax earnings, market penetration on the corporate side, good growth in retail savings and "excellent credit card performance" made for "a very satisfactory outcome".
Analysts had forecast pre-tax profits of between 345 and 383 million pounds for the first half and said that although UK banking profits were strong, overall results were no better than expected.
Royal Bank's shares dipped initially on the figures before recovering to stand three pence higher at 588-1/2 pence by early afternoon.
There had been some doubts about the performance of the bank's Direct Line insurance arm which showed a small profit increase to eight million pounds, from five million pounds.
Mathewson played down concerns about Direct Line, pointing out that predictions of "doomsday scenarios" were off the mark.

"Direct Line Insurance has retained profitability and we see signs in the market place that prices are beginning to recover and we expect our results this year we to be better than last year," he said.

Royal Bank's U.S. retail banking arm Citizens had performed well following its successful acquisition of First New Hampshire. Mathewson said Citizens had achieved natural growth of about eight percent in addition to this.
"The franchise continues to improve and we think we will continue to generate a lot of profit there," Mathewson said, adding he expected some further expansion through acquisition.

Mathewson said there are no immediate plans to increase Royal Bank's holding of Spain's Banco Santander but he hinted that Royal Bank would be expanding its operations in Europe beyond the project finance it currently offers.

Royal Bank's bad debt provision rose 32 million pounds to 77 million pounds but Mathewson said this was not an underlying trend because a year before it reflected a big write-back from Citizens and it now included formula driven provisions from the bank's credit card business.

And while the UK banking operations cost/income ratio, which fell by four percentage points, would continue to come down "in the fullness of time", the bank's custody business would increase it in the short term.
At the branch level rationalisation would continue, with the trend being towards fewer people working in branches but expansion in other areas, but no plans to cut branches.
Mathewson also dismissed any suggestion that Royal Bank might be taken over by a larger bank or merge with Bank of Scotland.

And while co-operation with Bank of Scotland where the result was financially beneficial to both parties was both logical and sensible, Mathewson said any suggestion of a merger was "fairyland", not least because the government would never allow such a concentration. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
